articles.title: Mark Zuckerberg's creative plan to pay California’s proposed billionaire tax without losing control of Meta | TechCrunch
articles.summary: A newly launched stock class being offered was partially engineered to help Meta founder and CEO Mark Zuckerberg pay the "billionaire's tax," should the measure be voted into law.
articles.body_text: During Meta’s earnings call on Wednesday, the company revealed its board had approved a new class of non-voting stock, called Class C common stock. The shares give the holder an ownership stake but no vote on company decisions. This class takes effect in January. Meta says it will use the stock for capital raising, employee pay, and acquisitions — including its expensive push into AI — while maintaining the current voting structure that favors its founder and CEO, Mark Zuckerberg, who controls around 60% of the vote. Now, however, the New York Times has reported there’s another reason for the new class: helping Zuckerberg pay for California’s proposed “billionaire tax,” if voters approve it. Because the new shares carry no votes, he could sell some of them to cover the tax without giving up voting control. Proposition 40 , which was drafted by Berkeley tax law professors and is being sponsored by California’s largest healthcare union (SEIU United Healthcare Workers West), would level a one-time 5% wealth tax on the net worth of several hundred California billionaires who primarily live in the state. Backers say the policy could generate as much as $100 billion over five years, the bulk of which would be used to pay for the state’s healthcare needs, with the rest for food assistance and education. The Times also reports that Zuckerberg pressed Meta’s board to come up with a plan to protect him from the tax. According to the paper, he told board members in September that if they couldn’t reach an agreement, he’d list his Palo Alto property for sale, potentially kicking off a media firestorm. Not long afterward, the stock plan materialized, the newspaper writes. The Times reporting is partially based on a recent SEC filing made by Meta, which documents the concern surrounding Proposition 40 and how it informed discussions that led to the new stock class. The filing says that as far back as July, Zuckerberg was discussing the billionaire tax with board members. The topic came up again in additional meetings and communications throughout that month and August. The filing also describes how the plan would work. Meta is creating a new class of non-voting shares, called Class C, and will give shareholders one of them for every Class A or Class B share they own. The company calls this a one-time stock dividend and says it should work out to a two-for-one stock split. The dividend “will not change the voting power of any shareholder,” Meta says. That is where Prop 40 comes in. The filing says the dividend “will allow Mr. Zuckerberg to immediately sell or transfer up to 20% of the shares of Class C common stock that he receives in the Dividend, representing 10% of his overall economic stake in the Company, for any reason, including so that he may pay his potential tax liability under California Proposition 40, if enacted into law, without affecting his majority voting control.” Because the dividend is one-for-one, half of his post-dividend shares will be Class C, so the 20% cap equals 10% of his total economic stake. When reached for comment by TechCrunch, Meta referred us to a quote included in its recent earnings press release that reiterates that part of the motivation for the creation of the stock was to keep Zuckerberg onboard: “The Special Committee affirmed its belief that it was important for Mr. Zuckerberg to continue to lead the Company from California, including because it was crucial that Mr. Zuckerberg remains in close coordination with the Company’s management and in close proximity to Meta Superintelligence Labs.” It’s been estimated that Zuckerberg would have to pay as much as $11 billion as part of the tax. Prop 40 has notably riled many of Silicon Valley’s most prominent businesspeople. Google co-founder Sergey Brin has aggressively campaigned against the measure, even spending a small fortune in an effort to defeat it. Other business leaders and critics of the proposal have criticized it online, with many claiming that it amounts to economic suicide for California, driving a capital flight from the state. However, as Meta’s new policy would appear to show, the state’s mega-companies and the people who run them have creative ways of dealing with the tax, should it materialize. “Looks like billionaires will stay and figure out a way to pay the tax,” Democratic U.S. Representative Ro Khanna, a vocal proponent of the tax, wrote on X, after news of Meta’s strategy spread online. “If we pass Prop 40, poor California kids can have healthcare,” he added.

articles.title: Warhound raises $200M to engineer war dogs and arm them with Anduril gear | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Warhound, the brainchild of Ben Lamm and Palmer Luckey, emerges from stealth to genetically engineer dogs for military and law enforcement.
articles.body_text: Colossal Biosciences’ Ben Lamm and Andruil’s Palmer Luckey had an idea to genetically engineer war dogs for the U.S. military, law enforcement, and other emergency response teams. That idea, on Thursday, announced its emergence from stealth as Warhound , armed with $200 million in funding from investors including In-Q-Tel, Sequoia, and 8VC. The round values the company at $1.2 billion. These are dogs that perform tasks that are dangerous for humans or difficult for machines, like bomb detection, searches, and other specialized operations. In its launch announcement, the company said that more than 80% of the working dogs used by the U.S. military come from Europe and less than half of them are fit for service. So not only is there a dwindling supply of working dogs for these tasks, but the U.S. has also become increasingly reliant on foreign nations for dogs that play an important role in the U.S. military and in law enforcement. That is key for what Warhound is trying to do. The hope is that Colossal can use its technology to engineer dogs with “characteristics suited to demanding missions,” the company said in a press release. Lamm told TechCrunch he met Luckey about a year ago at a conference, where the Anduril co-founder brought up doing more for working dogs in the U.S. military. The two kept in touch, and Lamm did more research, learning about the breeding issues. Many dogs do not make it through training because of genetic dispositions for issues like poor eyesight or the high possibilities of cancer, hip dysplasia, or muscle atrophy. Lamm believed dogs could be enhanced for health, longevity, and “for things like speed and agility or enhance olfactory sensors for bomb sniffing and whatnot,” he said. His team looked at the top-performing working dog breeds — the Belgian Malinois and German Shepherd — taking the cell lines from them and putting them in a biobank. From there, they will edit the genes, adding the ones that will make the dogs perform better while taking out the ones that won’t, to create “a new type of dog.” Andruil, meanwhile, will provide software and hardware enhancement for items such as dog protection vests and eye goggles to assist the dogs and their handlers with matters like situational awareness and coordination. He said to imagine, for example, bulletproof vests that have data sensors that give information back to the handlers so they can better understand what is happening. “The idea is, if we make the dog safer, make it healthier, make it perform better, it’s going to perform better in the line of duty,” Lamm said. He added that Anduril’s additions aim to make the dogs safer and healthier outside of their genetic components, “on top of the dog, not in the dog.” He believes such enhancements will also protect the dogs’ human handlers better. Luckey doesn’t own equity in the company and is only a partner, Lamm told TechCrunch, clarifying that Colossal owns equity in the business, which it supports with licensing its technology. Colossal is currently known for its de-extinction efforts of animals like the dodo and the mammoth . As Lamm previously told TechCrunch, the company has been using AI, buying and building technology to help with gene cloning and the identification and reproduction of animal genes. The first batch of dogs is about to be cloned and incubated and is expected to be born early next year, ideally entering service within the next two years, Lamm said. Another company owned by Colossal, Viagen, is partnering with Warhound to help clone the dogs. Lamm said Viagen’s tech has a high success rate with cloning, and Colossal currently uses it for its program to help protect endangered species. The startup doesn’t know yet how much it will charge for the dogs but expects to sell to parties like first responders, the Department of Defense, military service groups, and police forces. When asked about government approval, Lamm said the company has briefed many government groups about the business.

articles.title: As blockchain investing falls out of vogue, a16z Crypto rebrands as a16z Frontier | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The digital asset unit, helmed by Chris Dixon, broadens its scope.
articles.body_text: In a sign that crypto and blockchain-focused investing has receded in importance, Andreessen Horowitz announced Thursday that it is renaming its digital asset unit from a16z Crypto to a16z Frontier. The practice, helmed by Chris Dixon, has raised nearly $10 billion across five funds since launching in 2018, backing some of the sector’s biggest wins, including Coinbase. Yet for years, a16z and rival venture firms struggled to push crypto’s utility beyond financial rails, trading applications, and speculative assets. Under the new name, the team is broadening its mandate to focus on emerging technologies, be it AI, robotics, or “new kinds of networks” connecting humans and machines. Yet, the group isn’t abandoning crypto. Dixon wrote in a blog post that blockchain technology could “give new networks native economic capabilities.” Alongside Dixon, a16z Frontier’s general partners include Eddy Lazzarin and Guy Wuollet. Meanwhile, Ali Yahya, who joined the crypto strategy as its first investor in 2017, has left the firm, according to The Information . articles.title: Rivian buys world model startup to accelerate self-driving ambitions | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Third Dimension's technology uses AI to match the physical world, which when combined with Rivian's reams of data could turn into a valuable simulator.
articles.body_text: EV maker Rivian has acquired Third Dimension, a U.K. startup founded by veterans of the gaming and autonomous vehicle industries that uses AI to turn images and videos into lifelike 3D worlds. Rivian isn’t getting into gaming, but it does want to leverage Third Dimension’s technology to turn real-world data into 3D worlds that can accelerate the development of its advanced driver-assistance features and the self-driving system for the robotaxis it plans to supply to Uber . Terms of the deal were not disclosed. The 15-person team at Third Dimension, most of whom are based in the U.K., will be absorbed into Rivian’s autonomy and AI team led by James Philbin. The acquisition also gives Rivian an opportunity to expand its AI hub in London, Philbin said in an exclusive interview. Third Dimension, which was founded by CEO Tolga Kart and Piotr Sokólski in 2024, raised $7 million in seed funding from venture capital firms, including Abstract Ventures, MVP, Soma Capital, and Solari Capital. While the company’s technology was built to speed up video game development, the founders saw other potential applications, including defense and autonomous vehicles. Now, under Rivian, they’ll be focused on automated driving. Today, Rivian offers “Universal Hands-Free” driving software that lets drivers take their hands off the wheel on highways, while still watching the road. The company plans to, by the end of the year, release a version of the software that can handle the entire drive through surface streets and highways without touching the wheel, although the driver will still have to supervise and be ready to take over. Rivian is also working toward full autonomy, which it will deploy in the robotaxi versions of its R2 SUV that will be available on the Uber app in 2028. “The team is excited to be able to focus on one problem,” Kart told TechCrunch in an interview. “I think as a small company, having to serve many, many different masters is very hard, and so we’re very excited to come work on a problem that has such an amount of scale, where our technology makes a true difference.” Simulation is a critical tool for autonomous vehicle developers, who use it to train and validate self-driving systems. Historically, these simulators were built on rendering or video game engines and often relied on synthetic data. These virtual environments might look like the real world, but a gap between the two remains, Kart said. The workaround typically requires feeding the simulators ever-larger amounts of data in hopes of closing that quality gap. Third Dimension’s technology uses AI to match the physical world, which when combined with Rivian’s reams of data could turn into a valuable simulator. “For us, it’s about taking real scenarios, but making them simulatable,” Philbin said. “These are not synthetic kind of video game styles, they’re real things that happen in the world, but now we get that extra dial of being able to move the cameras around, shift other agents, have maybe different lighting or weather conditions. So it’s a really powerful tool for us.” It’s technology that Philbin said the company knew it wanted and had actually “done a pretty extensive kind of evaluation of a lot of different providers.” Any company developing automated driving technology needs data — and a lot of it. But the quality matters too. Real-world data collected from cameras and other sensors is especially valuable.

articles.title: 1Password launches a way for AI agents to log in on your behalf without seeing your password | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The new feature allows agents to log into a customer's personal accounts while still protecting the private credentials that secure those accounts.
articles.body_text: Concerns have swirled over the access that consumers are increasingly entrusting to AI agents. Now, security services are trying to catch up. Password manager 1Password on Thursday launched a new tool by which users can allow agents to log into their personal accounts on their behalf, without the agent ever having access to a user’s credentials. The new platform, dubbed 1Password for Agents , accomplishes this by creating a system of communication between the agent, the user, and the password manager. When an agent attempts to log in on a user’s behalf, a unique digital key is sent to 1Password to confirm the agent’s digital identity. The user is then sent an alert about the login attempt and can personally confirm the request. 1Password then signs in the agent, filling in the credentials on the digital assistant’s behalf, which allows it to log in and complete whatever task is at hand. 1Password for Agents allows users to choose their agent of choice — whether that’s Claude Duet from Anthropic, OpenAI’s Dots or ChatGPT Work, Grok Bot, Meta’s Muse, or agents from Town, which is an AI assistant startup. The company says it is working with other companies to expand the service. “Handing over a password, secret, or credential is a common shortcut to an agent, but can leave people with sensitive information in places they can no longer control as a copy gets saved for the next time,” the company said in a blog post . “1Password for Agents gives people a trusted way to delegate tasks to personal AI agents while keeping control of the passwords, secrets, and credentials those tasks require.” Online agentic activity has increasingly unsettled major institutions. Indeed, 1Password’s new platform is launching on the same day that Axios reports that U.S. banks have begun to detect agentic activity inside user accounts. This isn’t necessarily a case of rogue agents pilfering accounts but, rather, an example of how consumers are increasingly allowing automated services to act on their behalf, including on financial matters. However, the potential for agent-related problems is still large. The big issue appears to be that most banks cannot tell if the agentic activity is tied to user requests or not. Bankers interviewed by the outlet described the situation as “horrifying,” and a Chase spokesperson interviewed by Axios additionally told the outlet that customers “should not give their usernames and passwords to anyone.” When you purchase through links in our articles, we may earn a small commission . articles.title: OpenAI makes its Jev competitor widely available as decision model competition heats up | TechCrunch
articles.summary: OpenAI is launching its decision model to the world. Can it compete with the original Jev?
articles.body_text: OpenAI made its Decisions API model widely available to users for the first time, entering the market for fast, cheap intelligence that recently made TypeSafe, a startup founded by a former researcher at the frontier lab, a $7.6 billion company . TypeSafe’s Jev model created a category for deep learning models that act as super classifiers: Given a set of options, they can quickly make choices and offer a confidence rating in their decision. Software developers quickly found that these decision or System One models could replace LLMs in a variety of workflows, operating more quickly and a at dramatically lower cost. Nikunj Handa, the product lead for OpenAI’s APIs, told TechCrunch that his colleagues saw Jev and said “wow, we we have like a million use cases for this.” Handa’s team sprinted to offer their own version: Rather than building a specifically calibrated decision model, the team took ChatGPT Luna and reconfigured it to speed up the inference and lower the cost. “The big unlock with Decisions API has been the speed, shrinking things from one to three seconds to 100, 120, 180 milliseconds,” Handa said. “In the future, we may sort of like have specific training to make our models like even better in these ways. But right now, it’s just plain old Luna that gets the job done.” Announced at the company’s developer day on September 29, the Decisions API became available to all customers on Thursday. OpenAI added new voice and visual modalities to the public version, and worked to ensure lower latency in regions around the world by targeting its inference resources geographically. In initial trials with customers like Box, Datadog, Ramp, and Speak, engineers used the API to replace OpenAI’s LLMs with higher throughput. Andrew Hsu, the CTO at Speak, which builds AI language tutors, said the Decisions API allowed the company to cut the time between actions from 1.4 seconds to .13 seconds. OpenAI also used the product to improve their Dots voice assistant’s responsiveness. Still, it’s not clear exactly what makes a good decision model, other than “it works for you” — optimization across intelligence, cost, calibration, and speed seems to differ by workload. TypeSafe CEO Diogo Almeida distrusts benchmarks and urges people to trial the models in their own work, but even TypeSafe released its own rankings last week alongside the release of its latest Jev model, which includes new features including support for images and smart-if statements. Public benchmarks like the AIM System One Index and the Artificial Analysis Decision Index tend to favor D1 Ultra, a new decision model that Liquid released last week, and Base Lab’s Elephant-1. The latest Jev model remains competitive on both indices, in seventh and third, with OpenAI’s Decision Model falling eighth and fourteenth, respectively. However, TypeSafe’s offerings are, for now, the most widely-queried on OpenRouter. The most fun Jev benchmark, however, is JevMan , a benchmark where decision models play PacMan; the latest Jev model tops that ranking. Felix Wunderlich, the chief growth officer at Opper AI, which built the benchmark, said the classic game “is an interesting test because of its nonstop stream of quick, high-stakes decisions. At every junction the model must decide where to go in a few hundred milliseconds.” Where OpenAI’s arguably more capable model may have an advantage is in multi-modality—for image classification, “Luna is extremely powerful and has been showing better calibrations,” Handa told TechCrunch, adding that OpenAI customers want the Decisions API to be more flexible about using images as outputs as well. Handa also saw further increases in speed enabling new use cases: “Can we get this to something like you know 60 milliseconds, and then you could imagine like an API like call like for every single frame in like a video?” As these offerings get faster and cheaper, we can expect them to live up to Jev’s namesake, an economist who explained how using a resource more efficiently makes it more ubiquitous. Or, as Handa sees it, there will be an expanding “crazy set of use cases” that were hiding in plain sight until the decision models revealed them.

articles.title: Microsoft’s Mustafa Suleyman says its AI outperforms doctors on hard cases as he chases ‘medical superintelligence’ | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Microsoft’s new AI diagnostic system beat generalist doctors on hard cases, according to a study in Science. But most of the improvement seems to come from the AI models underneath, not from Microsoft’s system itself.
articles.body_text: Microsoft’s AI diagnostic system correctly diagnosed complex medical cases in a simulation more than twice as often as generalist physicians, according to a study published Thursday in Science. Mustafa Suleyman, Microsoft AI’s CEO, called the result a step toward “medical superintelligence.” The system, dubbed MAI-DxO (DxO for short), coordinates several AI agents that act like a panel of doctors. They question a patient, order tests, and debate a diagnosis. In a simulation using complex cases from the New England Journal of Medicine, it was correct 83% of the time. Primary care doctors and general internists, working individually with reference materials, were correct 36% of the time. One note: Cases this complex are usually handled by specialists or physician teams, who weren’t part of the comparison. “There is something very substantial and exciting here,” Dominic King, vice president of Health at Microsoft AI, told TechCrunch. “The biggest challenge in healthcare delivery at the moment is the growing mismatch between demand and supply of medical expertise.” In publishing these results , Microsoft joins Go o gle and OpenAI in claiming that its AI can match or outperform doctors. The study’s own data suggests that much of the improvement comes from more powerful underlying AI models, with Microsoft’s orchestration system adding gains on top. Microsoft tested MAI-DxO with models from several companies, including OpenAI, Google, Anthropic, Meta, and DeepSeek, but its best results came with OpenAI’s GPT-5 and GPT-5.5. Microsoft measured DxO on cost as well as accuracy, meaning the estimated cost of running the AI on each case. On its own with a short, basic prompt, GPT-5 scored 78.9% on complex cases at about $8,400 per case. DxO cut that cost by about $3,000 but raised accuracy by only about four points. On emergency department cases, there was little improvement in either accuracy or cost improvement between GPT-5 on its own and with the assist from DxO. With GPT-5.5, a newer model released in April 2026, the results split. On complex cases, DxO increased GPT-5.5’s accuracy score from 72% to nearly 87% at a slightly cheaper cost. However, the gains once again didn’t show up on emergency department cases. Both (with and without DxO) scored about 85% at a similar cost. DxO helps most on complex cases and with less capable AI models. Gemini 2.5 Flash, for example, scored 46.4% on its own but nearly 69% with DxO. Even so, the gap between the weaker and stronger models was larger than the boost DxO provided. Microsoft’s researchers said that accuracy gains naturally shrink as models approach the theoretical maximum. “The DxO orchestration helps with the broader challenge of optimization both accuracy and cost,” a spokesperson added. Suleyman, who leads Microsoft’s effort to build its own frontier AI, told TechCrunch that the company is working with the Mayo Clinic to train a foundation model for healthcare, with release planned for next year. He believes this model will enable the company to “make really enormous leaps here,” and says DxO is part of the foundational infrastructure Microsoft is building to see real breakthroughs in healthcare.

articles.title: Tesla is prepping a Cybercab onslaught | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The company is looking to roll out the gold two-seater robotaxis to other U.S. cities this year, even as it goes mum on the number of paid rides.
articles.body_text: Tesla says it is preparing to launch its shiny gold Cybercab in new markets outside its home of Austin, Texas, in a bid to “literally take over every part of terrestrial transportation.” “We’re starting with getting people from one place to the other, but we want to basically own transportation of any kind on Earth,” Chief Financial Officer Vaibhav Taneja said on the company’s third-quarter earnings call Wednesday. Tesla has previously shown a concept version of a multi-passenger vehicle it calls the “Robovan,” but it’s unclear if Taneja’s bombastic comments mean the company is working on other types of transportation. What was clearer on the call is that Tesla’s Cybercab expansion will begin in Dallas next month and spread to other cities by the end of this year. Tesla already operates robotaxi versions of its Model Y SUV in small fleets in Dallas, Houston, and the Florida cities of Miami, Orlando, and Tampa. The company also said on its earnings call that it will start selling Cybercabs to fleet operators by the end of this year . Broader expansion of the Cybercab could set up a real fight with Waymo, which is currently the market leader for robotaxis in the United States, with more than 4,000 of them deployed across more than a dozen cities. Tesla has argued that its Cybercab is cheaper and easier to build, which should allow it to undercut Waymo and other robotaxi operators on price. But the company has to reach real scale outside Austin in order to prove that point. Tesla said it’s ready thanks to a dramatic increase in the number of miles its self-driving cars have traveled in recent weeks. While that may be true, Tesla was mum on Wednesday about how much money the overall robotaxi effort is bringing in. Tesla CEO Elon Musk said the new ride-hailing business won’t be noticeable in the company’s overall financial figures until the second quarter of 2027, “and probably a big deal by Q3 or Q4 of next year.” Tesla also made a change to its letter to shareholders that further obscures what little visibility there was into its robotaxi business. In Tesla’s second-quarter letter, the company included a chart for “Cumulative Paid Robotaxi Miles.” A close read of that chart showed a 36% decline from the first quarter of the year. In the new letter released on Wednesday, Tesla changed that chart to show “Cumulative Unsupervised Robotaxi Miles” — an indicator of how far the fleet cars are driving, whether or not they have paying riders on board. There wasn’t much more clarity on the call, either. When asked about paid robotaxi miles traveled, Taneja said the company is “seeing utilization improving,” but didn’t offer specifics. Instead, Taneja kept most of his comments generally focused on Tesla’s plans to scale the Cybercab. That included praise for Tesla’s engineering team for creating a vehicle that, according to the manufacturing team, is very easy to build — and build quickly. “They think this is one of the easiest products for them to scale in terms of manufacturing,” he said. “So scaling would not be that much of a challenge.” What might be a challenge, Taneja said, is that Tesla needs to make sure it has “all the regulatory approvals” so it can “start deploying the Cybercabs as fast as we can produce them.” That echoes many previous comments from Musk, who has long claimed that “regulatory approval” was the biggest barrier to Tesla’s robotaxi plans, not technical progress.

articles.title: Fusion startup Helion is developing new semiconductors that could double output of its power plants | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Helion now has another $225 million to help speed development of its first fusion power plant, due to provide Microsoft with electricity in 2028.
articles.body_text: Fusion startup Helion has been awarded $175 million in federal funding to research, develop, and manufacture advanced semiconductors and power electronics for its fusion power plants, the company announced on Thursday. Currently, those devices lose about 5% to 10% of the electricity that flows through them. While those losses seem small, they can compound themselves in a complex system like Helion’s. “If we can cut that loss in half, that’s actually twice the power output of the fusion system,” David Kirtley, co-founder and CEO at Helion, told TechCrunch. Helion has been racing to complete its first power plant, Orion, in time to meet a 2028 deadline to provide Microsoft with electricity from the grid. Funding from the award will help Helion build automated semiconductor module, packaging, and testing capacity to supply the fusion machine that’s currently under construction. The new production line, to be built in Washington State, will be the first in the U.S. to make a class of semiconductor that is used not just in fusion power, but in manufacturing, wastewater treatment, medicine, and defense. “There are no U.S. manufacturers right now that do it,” Kirtley said. “This is absolutely enabling going from zero to 100 for advanced, high-voltage, and pulsed semiconductors here in the United States.” The three-year award was made by the Department of Commerce under the CHIPS Act, a Biden-era law that seeks to bolster semiconductor module research, development, and manufacturing in the U.S. Alongside the federal funding, Helion also announced a fresh $50 million private investment, though it didn’t disclose the investor. In total, Helion has raised more than $3.2 billion, making it the second-best-funded fusion startup . More than $100 million will be set aside for semiconductor and advanced packaging R&D in Washington State, while approximately $80 million will support R&D efforts in Vermont for advanced semiconductor tooling, design, and process development with GlobalFoundries, Kirtley told TechCrunch. Separately, GlobalFoundries has received more than $80 million from the federal government to advance the manufacturing of gallium-nitride semiconductors, a type that is widely used in power electronics. Kirtley acknowledged that the R&D funded by the award won’t make its way into Orion in time for the launch — federal contracts can take months to negotiate — but he said they promise to help improve the efficiency of subsequent Helion power plants, which would improve their competitiveness in cutthroat electricity markets. Semiconductor efficiency is key to Helion’s approach to fusion, which harvests electricity directly from the fusion reactions rather than using them to heat steam to spin a turbine. The startup is developing a reactor known as a field-reversed configuration. Fusion fuel gets injected into both ends of an hourglass-like chamber, where it’s heated to form a plasma. The plasmas are then accelerated toward each other using magnetic fields. When they collide, another magnetic field compresses the ball further, raising the temperature to over 100 million degrees C. At those temperatures and pressures, atoms in the fusion fuel start fusing, releasing energy in the process, and pushing the plasma outward. This force pushes against the magnetic field, and that energy is captured by the magnets and capacitors and turned into electricity — think of how a hybrid car or EV recharges the battery by using electric motors to slow the vehicle.

articles.title: Elon Musk got $1 billion from Larry Ellison for his Twitter takeover
articles.summary: Elon Musk told the SEC he has lined up over $7 billion in funding to support his Twitter purchase. Key names include Larry Ellison, Prince Alwaleed bin Talal, Andreessen Horowitz, Binance, and the state investment firm of Qatar.
articles.body_text: Elon Musk has secured $7.1 billion in new financing for his takeover of Twitter — which CNBC reports will include assuming the role of “temporary CEO” — with this round of funding coming from a group of sometimes high-profile outside investors. At the top of the list is Larry Ellison, with the co-founder and current CTO of Oracle committing $1 billion to the purchase. Ellison has said that he is “very close friends” with Musk, and he was added to Tesla’s board in 2018. As one of the richest people alive — a superlative he shares with Musk — and an estimated net worth of over $100 billion, the investment is relatively small change for him. Back in 2012, Ellison bought nearly the entire Hawaiian island of Lanai for around $500 million. The new list of investors also includes the venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz, the financial firm Fidelity, the crypto exchange Binance, and the state investment firm of Qatar. Saudi Prince Alwaleed bin Talal also agreed to remain invested in Twitter after the deal closes — despite initially saying that Musk’s offer doesn’t “[come] close to the intrinsic value of Twitter” and saying he would reject the buyout. As the merger closes, his nearly $1.9 billion stake in Twitter will be rolled over into an investment into the private company. [Media: https://twitter.com/bhorowitz/status/1522198628244156416] Now, the prince tweeted to his “new” friend Elon: “I believe you will be an excellent leader for Twitter to propel & maximise its great potential.” Binance boss Changpeng Zhao told the Financial Times that his company’s $500 million buy-in is “more of a blank check” than an investment based on any specific plans. Andreessen Horowitz co-founder Ben Horowitz posted several tweets about why his firm is investing $400 million, criticizing unspecified incidents of censorship and saying “we believe in Ev and Jack’s vision to connect the world and we believe in Elon’s brilliance to finally make it what it was meant to be.” Horowitz blamed some of the problems on Twitter being a public company reliant on advertising and got a co-sign from its former CEO and co-founder Jack Dorsey, who tweeted “this is true. it needs cover for a while.” Musk reached an agreement with Twitter last week to take the company private for $44 billion. The new funding allows Musk to commit less of his own wealth to the deal, which may be important for him since much of that money is tied up in Tesla stock. The acquisition is expected to close later this year. Musk has thus far offered vague and sometimes lofty details about how he’ll change Twitter, from “authenticating all humans” to pulling its business away from advertising. Mostly, he’s said he wants the platform to be a forum for free speech, though it remains unclear what that means in practice. Musk has also said buying Twitter “is not a way to make money.” But he’s also reported to be considering job cuts and charging businesses and governments to use the platform. Flera delstater kan stämmas – och han utesluter inte att blockera valresultat. – Självklart finns det scenarier som vi skulle kunna föreställa oss det, säger han. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. USA:s justitieminister Todd Blanche hotar med rättsliga åtgärder mot fler delstater inför mellanårsvalet. Han säger också att regeringen i vissa lägen kan ingripa i valprocessen om de anser att det behövs. Demokraterna säger att de har förberett sig i månader och tänker kämpa mot varje försök att påverka valresultatet. I förra veckan stämde Trumpadministrationen Kalifornien för en påstådd ”brist på att vilja samarbeta med den federala regeringen för att skydda tillförlitligheten i våra val”. Bakgrunden var en plötslig åtgärd där justitiedepartementet krävde att delstaten inom 48 timmar skulle gå igenom en lista med, enligt departementet, 20 000 namn och säkerställa att personerna är amerikanska medborgare. Nu hotar justitieminister Todd Blanche med liknande åtgärder på andra håll. – Det finns ett antal delstater som vi kollar på, säger han på en pressträff. – Vi har tydliga bevis på att det finns folk på listorna som inte har rätt att rösta. Administrationen har inte presenterat några detaljer om hur slutsatserna dragits. Donald Trump har länge hävdat att det är ett utbrett problem med icke-medborgare som röstar, vilket inte har något som helst stöd i forskningen. I somras påstod administrationen att de hittat 15 903 personer på vallistorna i Nevada som inte är medborgare – en siffra som sedan sänktes till 185 och därefter slutade på noll. Andra liknande påståenden har inte heller kunnat beläggas.

articles.title: Två till sjukhus efter allvarlig olycka på E6
articles.summary: En bil körde under torsdagskvällen i fel riktning på E6. Två personer har förts till sjukhus efter en frontalkrock och vägen har varit avstängd sedan 21-tiden.
articles.body_text: En bil körde under torsdagskvällen i fel riktning på E6. Två personer har förts till sjukhus efter en frontalkrock och vägen har varit avstängd sedan 21-tiden. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Vid 21 tiden under torsdagen larmades polis, räddningstjänst och ambulans efter att två bilar frontalkrockat på E6 i höjd med Lockarp utanför Malmö. – Det är en bil som kört på motorvägen i fel riktning och frontalkrockat med en annan personbil. Det var en kraftig kollision, säger Björn Gerlach, vakthavande befäl vid räddningstjänsten Syd. Person som kört i fel riktning blev fastklämd i sin bil. Räddningstjänst arbetade i en timme med att få loss föraren ur bilen. Efter att de klippt av taket lyckades de få ut honom ur bilen. Då var han vaken och talbar. – Även den andra föraren fördes till sjukhus men enligt våra uppgifter var han ute och gick, säger Gerlach. Båda personerna fördes till sjukhus efter olyckan med okänt skadeläge. Även en hund ska ha befunnit sig i en av bilarna, den fördes till djursjukhus. Efter olyckan stängdes E6 av i riktning mot Köpenhamn medan arbete pågick på platsen. Sydsvenskan skriver att vägen öppnade strax innan midnatt. Olyckan inträffade på E6 och vägen är avstängd i riktning mot Köpenhamn medan arbete pågår på platsen. Trafiken leds om, skriver Sydsvenskan. Detta är en nyhetsartikel. Men ledaren Jevgenij Prigozjin kom inte överens med Kreml, och ett myteri uppstod. Trupperna avbröt marschen söder om Moskva, men Prigozjins relation med Putin var så gott som förstörd. Några månader senare sprängdes Prigozjins plan i luften. Nu rapporterar Wall Street Journal att gruppen fortsätter att operera i Afrika – nu under ledning av Prigozjins son Pavel, 28. – Jag antar att Pavel fick tillstånd att fortsätta verksamheten, vilket innebär att han förmedlade en överenskommelse med Kreml eller på annat sätt gjordes ofarlig, säger utredaren Lou Osborn till WSJ. Wagnergruppen och pappa Prigozjin var aktiva i Afrika redan innan hans död där de anställdes av regimer för att agera legosoldater. Men Wagners roll är en annan i dag, enligt Osborn. I stället ägnar man sig åt att agera vapen- och droghandlare, primärt till rebellgrupper i Sudan och Libyen, två länder med varsitt inbördeskrig. Enligt WSJ har Pavel Prigozjin även expanderat gruppens bas i Centralafrikanska republikens huvudstad Bangui, och agerar fortfarande livvakter åt landets diktator Faustin-Archange Touadéra. Prigozjinfamiljens imperium, som innehåller både laglig och olaglig verksamhet, är värd drygt fyra miljarder kronor.

articles.title: Polis hittade död man – låtsades vara honom i år
articles.summary: En polis i USA hittade en äldre man död i sitt hem 2022. Då tog han över mannens hus – och låtsades att han levde.
articles.body_text: En polis i USA hittade en äldre man död i sitt hem 2022. Då tog han över mannens hus – och låtsades att han levde. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Under en kontroll i juli 2022 hittade polismannen Brian Sguros den 71-årige mannen Dennis West död i sin bostad i Florida . Men det var information som Sguros försökte hålla hemlig. Han inledde då sin komplexa plan för att ta över den döda mannens hus – genom att låtsats att han vore vid liv. Det rapporterar The Telegraph . Veckor efter att Sguros upptäckt West tog han olovligen över hans bostad. Han städade, reparerade och renoverade huset fram till 2025. Totalt spenderade han 214 000 dollar på ombyggnation. Bland annat bytte han dörrar och fönster. Under tiden som renoveringen pågick betalade Sguros den döda mannens skatter och räkningar i hans namn. Han höll också Wests identitet aktiv för att få det att se ut som att han fortfarande levde. Genom polisens egna databaser samlade han information om honom. Bedrägeriet uppdagades efter att Sguros och hans partner försökt hävda laglig rätt över bostaden. Brian Sguros greps i tisdags och har nu åtalats för flera brott. Bland annat tjänstefel, dataintrång, och flera bedrägeribrott kopplat till identitetsstölden. Till sitt försvar säger Sguros att han tog över bostaden för att det var ”säkerhetsrisk” och att han ville förhindra personer från att olovligen bosätta sig där. Sguros fick sparken från sitt polisjobb i samband med gripandet. Nu väntar rättegång. Men Sguros kräver pengar tillbaka för kostnaden han lade på renoveringen. Detta är en nyhetsartikel. articles.title: Trumps hemliga plan: ”Katastrof”
articles.summary: Miljontals amerikaner riskerar att få sina löner och skatteåterbäringar beslagtagna. Trumpadministrationen förbereder nya åtgärder mot personer som inte betalar sina studielån, rapporterar The Washington Sun.
articles.body_text: Miljontals amerikaner riskerar att få sina löner och skatteåterbäringar beslagtagna. Trumpadministrationen förbereder nya åtgärder mot personer som inte betalar sina studielån, rapporterar The Washington Sun . Men planerna väntas hållas hemliga till efter mellanårsvalet. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Nästan tio miljoner amerikaner som inte betalar sina federala studielån kan snart få det hett om öronen. Enligt fem källor som The Washington Sun har talat med förbereder Trumpadministrationen sig för att återuppta indrivningen av obetalda studieskulder under 2027. Finansdepartementet planerar bland annat att anlita privata inkassoföretag, möjligen redan i november. I verktygslådan finns bland annat möjligheten att driva in skulder genom att hålla inne skatteåterbäringar och vissa andra federala ersättningar, men också att kräva att arbetsgivare drar pengar direkt från anställdas löner. Planerna på att återuppta tvångsindrivningen efter coronapandemin presenterades redan våren 2025, men har sedan dess skjutits upp vid flera tillfällen. En orsak är att tjänstemän på finansdepartementet har varnat för att åtgärderna riskerar att slå hårt mot framför allt låginkomsttagare, däribland många av Trumps egna väljare. Det är också därför ett offentligt besked om planerna inte väntas förrän efter mellanårsvalet den 3 november, skriver The Washington Sun. – Det vore politiskt vansinnigt att genomföra detta före mellanårsvalet, säger en av källorna till tidningen.

articles.summary: Är Van Goghs världsberömda himmel fantasi eller verklighet? Nu tror sig forskare funnit svaret.
articles.body_text: Är Van Goghs världsberömda himmel fantasi eller verklighet? Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Under lång tid har man trott att Vincent van Goghs berömda verk ”Stjärnenatt” skapades ur den nederländske konstnärens fantasi. Men icke, enligt ny forskning från Sydkorea, som menar att målningen matchar en himmel runt den 22 juli 1889. Det skriver The Guardian . Då var van Gogh inlagd på ett mentalsjukhus i sydfranska Saint-Rémy-de- Provence efter att han lagt in sig själv på grund av sitt dåliga psykiska mående. Tidigare har man trott att han målade Stjärnenatt i juni, vilket grundat sig i ett brev som konstnären skickade till sin bror runt den 18 juni samma år. Där i ska han ha beskrivit ”en ny studie av stjärnhimmel”. Dessutom ska han ha haft ett mentalt sammanbrott i juli, vilket man tror gjorde honom inkapabel att måla under flera veckor. Men nu tror forskarna alltså att målningen är en månad äldre och en överdriven verklighet snarare än ren fantasi. Forskarna har tagit sig till mentalsjukhuset och matchat en skiss med landskapet runtom. Det exakta datumet, den 22 juli, har forskarna kommit fram till genom en programvara för astrologi där de återskapat gryningshimlar varje dag i juni och varje dag i juli under 1889. Den 22 juli var då den gryning som matchade bäst. Forskarna förtydligar också att van Gogh givetvis kan ha tagit inspiration från flera dagars himlar. Detta är en nyhetsartikel. articles.body_text: Airbnbs nya regler får flera stugvärdar att rasa. – Jag tycker ”mitt hus, mina regler”, säger Ulf Eriksson, som hyr ut bostäder i bland annat i Norrtälje. Nu vill flera uthyrare lämna plattformen. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. ■ Enligt Airbnbs nya regler får inte värdar kräva att gästerna diskar eller tar ut soporna. ■ Svenska uthyrare rasar nu över minskat självbestämmande. ■ Flera uppges hota med att lämna plattformen – och det kan bli högre priser. Airbnb stramar åt reglerna för sina uthyrare. Framöver får stugvärdar till exempel inte kräva att gästerna diskar, tar av sängkläder eller tar ut sopor. Detta har fått uthyrare i Sverige att ilskna till. En av dem är Ulf Eriksson, 53. Han började hyra ut i mindre skala som en hobby för cirka tio år sen men hyr numera, tillsammans med sin fru Lena, ut totalt sju bostäder i Norrtälje, Västervik och Järvsö. Han fick ett mejl med Airbnbs nya policy för husregler på onsdagen. – Det blir mindre och mindre självbestämmande för oss värdar. Att jag inte kan be gästerna sätta i gång diskmaskinen eller slänga sopor i en soptunna utanför huset, eller strippa sängarna på sängkläder. På sin hemsida skriver Airbnb att värdar inte kan be sina gäster, som betalar städavgift, utföra uppgifter som ”normalt skulle utföras av en städare”.
